sentences.nl: Mijn naam is Bart de Pau,, online docent Nederlands.
sentences.en: My name is Bart de Pau, online Dutch teacher.

sentences.nl: Vandaag oefenen we Nederlandse zinnen, met de grammatica van #dutchgrammar-2 les 23, over onregelmatige werkwoorden.
sentences.en: Today we are practicing Dutch sentences, with the grammar from #dutchgrammar-2 lesson 23, about irregular verbs.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Today practice we Dutch sentences, with the grammar of #dutchgrammar-2 lesson 23, about irregular verbs.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Vandaag" (Today) indicates the time and is placed at the beginning for emphasis.  
• "Oefenen we" (practice we) shows the verb-second word order typical in Dutch main clauses.  
• "Met de grammatica van" (with the grammar of) uses "met" to indicate accompaniment or inclusion.  
• "Over onregelmatige werkwoorden" (about irregular verbs) uses "over" to introduce the topic.  

Extra examples:  
– "Morgen leren we nieuwe woorden." (Tomorrow we learn new words.)  
– "We praten over de geschiedenis van Nederland." (We talk about the history of the Netherlands.)  
– "Met de hulp van een vriend, maakte ik de opdracht af." (With the help of a friend, I finished the assignment.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Volgende week bespreken we de cultuur van Nederland, met de nadruk op tradities. (Next week we discuss the culture of the Netherlands, with an emphasis on traditions.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• #dutchgrammar is a popular online resource for learning Dutch, and it often organizes its lessons into structured series, such as "les 23" (lesson 23), which is a common way to reference specific lessons in educational contexts.

sentences.nl: De studenten zijn gisteren tijdens de les, naar het museumdorp Orvelte geweest.
sentences.en: The students went to the museum village Orvelte during the class yesterday.

sentences.nl: Ze vertrokken om 11 uur met de fiets.
sentences.en: They left at 11 o'clock by bicycle.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• They left at 11 o'clock with the bicycle.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ze vertrokken" is in the past tense (simple past) and means "They left."  
• "Om 11 uur" means "at 11 o'clock," using "om" to indicate a specific time.  
• "Met de fiets" means "with the bicycle," using "met" to indicate the means of transportation.  
• Example 1: "Ze komen om 3 uur aan." (They arrive at 3 o'clock.)  
• Example 2: "We gaan met de auto." (We are going by car.)  
• Example 3: "Hij vertrok om 9 uur." (He left at 9 o'clock.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ze komen om 6 uur met de trein." (They arrive at 6 o'clock by train.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Cycling is a common mode of transportation in the Netherlands, often used for commuting to work, school, or just for leisure activities.

sentences.nl: Gelukkig scheen de zon,, want eerder die ochtend was het slecht weer.
sentences.en: Fortunately, the sun was shining, because earlier that morning the weather was bad.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Luckily shone the sun, because earlier that morning was it bad weather.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Gelukkig" (Luckily) is an adverb describing the manner in which the sun was shining.  
• "scheen" is the past tense of "schijnen" (to shine).  
• "want" is a coordinating conjunction meaning "because," introducing a reason.  
• The phrase "was het slecht weer" (was it bad weather) follows standard Dutch word order: subject-verb-complement.

Examples:  
- "Gelukkig regende het niet." (Luckily it did not rain.)  
- "Want ik had een paraplu nodig." (Because I needed an umbrella.)  
- "Eerder die avond ging hij naar huis." (Earlier that evening he went home.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Gelukkig hadden we een reservering, want het restaurant was vol." (Luckily we had a reservation, because the restaurant was full.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No specific cultural note applies here.

sentences.nl: Het was maar een kwartiertje fietsen,, dus om kwart over 11 kwamen ze aan.
sentences.en: It was only a fifteen-minute bike ride, so they arrived at a quarter past 11.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• It was only a little quarter-hour cycling, so at quarter past 11 came they arrive.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Het was maar een kwartiertje fietsen" uses "maar" to mean "only," and "kwartiertje" is a diminutive form of "kwartier" (quarter-hour) indicating a short period.  
• "Fietsen" is an infinitive used as a noun here, meaning "cycling" or "biking."  
• "Om kwart over 11" indicates time, using "om" for "at" and "kwart over" meaning "quarter past."  
• "Kwamen ze aan" is in the past tense (simple past) and follows the subject-verb inversion typical in subordinate clauses or sentences starting with a time element.  
• Example 1: "Het was maar een uurtje wachten." (It was only an hour waiting.)  
• Example 2: "Om half 8 vertrok de trein." (At half past 7, the train departed.)  
• Example 3: "Na een lange dag werken, kwam hij thuis." (After a long day of working, he came home.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Het was maar een klein stukje lopen, dus om 9 uur waren we er." (It was only a small walk, so at 9 o'clock we were there.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, cycling is a very common mode of transportation, and distances are often described by the time it takes to bike them rather than in kilometers or miles. It's common to hear phrases like "een kwartiertje fietsen" in daily conversation.

sentences.nl: Marieke gaf de studenten een opdracht:, het voorbereiden van een spreekbeurt.
sentences.en: Marieke gave the students an assignment: preparing a speech.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Marieke gave the students an assignment: preparing for a presentation.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Gaf" is the past tense of "geven" (to give), showing a completed action.  
• "De studenten" is the indirect object, and "een opdracht" is the direct object. In Dutch, the indirect object often precedes the direct object.  
• "Het voorbereiden van een spreekbeurt" is a noun phrase introduced by "het," a neuter definite article, which is used to turn the verb "voorbereiden" (to prepare) into a noun.  

Examples:  
– "Hij gaf zijn vriendin een cadeau." (He gave his girlfriend a gift.)  
– "Zij stuurde haar ouders een kaart." (She sent her parents a card.)  
– "Het lezen van boeken is zijn hobby." (Reading books is his hobby.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Leraar gaf de klas een project: het maken van een maquette." (The teacher gave the class a project: building a model.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch education, presentations (spreekbeurten) are a common assignment, encouraging public speaking skills from an early age.

sentences.nl: Ze maakte 2 groepen van 4 studenten.
sentences.en: She made 2 groups of 4 students.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• She made 2 groups of 4 students.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• **Ze maakte**: "Ze" means "she," and "maakte" is the past tense of "maken" (to make). The simple past tense is used here.  
• **2 groepen**: "2" is a numeral, and "groepen" is the plural of "groep" (group). Dutch often places numerals before the noun.  
• **van 4 studenten**: "van" means "of," indicating a partitive relationship. "Studenten" is the plural of "student" (student).

Extra sentences:  
• Ze maakte een taart voor het feest. (She made a cake for the party.)  
• Hij maakte een lijst van de benodigdheden. (He made a list of the necessities.)  
• We vormen twee teams van vijf mensen. (We form two teams of five people.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Ze deelde de klas in drie groepen. (She divided the class into three groups.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch schools and universities, group work is quite common. Students often work in groups for projects, which can lead to the division of classes into smaller groups as described in the sentence.

sentences.nl: Anika, Jenn, Pablo en Xing zaten in de eerste groep.
sentences.en: Anika, Jenn, Pablo, and Xing were in the first group.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Anika, Jenn, Pablo and Xing sat in the first group.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "zaten" is the past tense of "zitten" (to sit). Dutch uses the simple past tense to describe completed actions.  
• "in de eerste groep" means "in the first group," using the preposition "in" to indicate location or position.  
• The word order follows a simple Subject-Verb-Object structure.

Extra phrases:  
• Zij zaten aan de tafel. (They sat at the table.)  
• Hij zat naast zijn vriend. (He sat next to his friend.)  
• Wij zaten op het gras. (We sat on the grass.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Maria en Tom zaten in de tweede rij. (Maria and Tom sat in the second row.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No specific cultural note applies to this sentence.

sentences.nl: Gianluca, Soliman, Kathy en Lars zaten in de tweede groep.
sentences.en: Gianluca, Soliman, Kathy, and Lars were in the second group.

sentences.nl: De eerste groep moest naar de klompenmakerij.
sentences.en: The first group had to go to the clog maker.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The first group had to to the clog-making workshop.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "De eerste groep" (The first group) acts as the subject.  
• "moest" is the past tense of "moeten" (must/have to), indicating obligation or necessity in the past.  
• "naar" is a preposition meaning "to," used here to indicate direction towards a place.  
• "de klompenmakerij" (the clog-making workshop) is a compound noun, combining "klompen" (clogs) and "makerij" (workshop/factory).

• Extra Phrases:  
  - "De tweede groep moest naar de molen." (The second group had to go to the mill.)  
  - "Wij moesten naar het strand gisteren." (We had to go to the beach yesterday.)  
  - "Zij moest naar de dokter na het ongeluk." (She had to go to the doctor after the accident.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "De derde groep moest naar het museum." (The third group had to go to the museum.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Klompen (clogs) are traditional Dutch wooden shoes. Visiting a klompenmakerij is a common activity for tourists to learn about this aspect of Dutch heritage.

sentences.nl: De tweede groep ging naar de smederij.
sentences.en: The second group went to the forge.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The second group went to the smithy.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "De tweede groep" (The second group): "de" is the definite article, "tweede" is an ordinal number, and "groep" is a noun.  
• "ging" (went): past tense of "gaan" (to go). Dutch uses simple past tense for completed actions.  
• "naar" (to): preposition used for directions or destinations.  
• "de smederij" (the smithy): "de" is the definite article, "smederij" is a noun.  

Extra sentences:  
• "De eerste groep ging naar de markt." (The first group went to the market.)  
• "De derde groep ging naar het museum." (The third group went to the museum.)  
• "Zij ging naar de bakker." (She went to the baker.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "De vierde groep ging naar het park." (The fourth group went to the park.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Historically, a "smederij" or smithy was a common feature in Dutch villages and towns, where a blacksmith would create and repair metal items.

sentences.nl: De studenten kregen een rondleiding.
sentences.en: The students were given a tour.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The students received a tour.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The verb "kregen" is in the past tense, plural form of "krijgen" (to receive).  
• "Een rondleiding" translates to "a tour," where "rondleiding" is a compound noun formed from "rond" (around) and "leiding" (guiding).  
• Dutch word order typically places the subject first, followed by the verb, then the object.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "De kinderen kregen cadeaus." (The children received gifts.)  
  - "Hij kreeg een medaille." (He received a medal.)  
  - "Wij kregen een uitnodiging." (We received an invitation.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• De toeristen kregen een uitgebreide uitleg. (The tourists received a detailed explanation.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Tours and guided visits, especially in museums or historical sites, are common in Dutch culture, given the country's rich history and focus on education.

sentences.nl: Ze schreven alles op, en ze vroegen veel aan de gids.
sentences.en: They wrote everything down, and they asked the guide a lot of questions.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• They wrote everything down, and they asked a lot to the guide.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ze schreven alles op" uses the past tense ("schreven") with a separable verb ("opschrijven," to write down).  
• "En ze vroegen veel aan de gids" uses the past tense of "vragen" (vroegen) and includes the preposition "aan" to indicate whom they asked.  
• Example 1: "Hij schreef de notities op." (He wrote the notes down.)  
• Example 2: "Wij vroegen de docent veel vragen." (We asked the teacher many questions.)  
• Example 3: "Zij vroegen om hulp aan de buren." (They asked the neighbors for help.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Ze luisterden aandachtig naar de gids en schreven alles op. (They listened attentively to the guide and wrote everything down.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, it is common for visitors to participate actively in guided tours by asking questions and taking notes, reflecting a general cultural value placed on learning and engagement.

sentences.nl: Ze moesten wel goed luisteren,, want de gids sprak met een Drents accent.
sentences.en: They had to listen carefully because the guide spoke with a Drents accent.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• They had to really listen well, because the guide spoke with a Drents accent.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ze moesten wel goed luisteren" uses "moesten," the past tense of "moeten," indicating necessity or obligation. "Wel" adds emphasis, suggesting they really had to listen carefully.  
• "want" is a coordinating conjunction meaning "because," explaining the reason for the action.  
• "met een Drents accent" describes the manner of speaking, using "met" (with) to indicate accompaniment and "Drents accent" specifying the regional dialect.

Examples:  
• "Ze moesten wel snel lopen, want de trein vertrok bijna." (They really had to walk fast, because the train was about to leave.)  
• "Hij moet wel harder werken, want de deadline is morgen." (He really has to work harder, because the deadline is tomorrow.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• De kinderen moesten wel stil zijn, want de leraar was aan het uitleggen. (The children really had to be quiet, because the teacher was explaining.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The Drents accent refers to the dialect spoken in Drenthe, a province in the Netherlands. It is one of many regional accents and dialects in the country, each with its unique features. Understanding these can be important for effective communication in different regions.

sentences.nl: Daardoor verstonden ze niet alles,, hoewel ze het meeste wel begrepen.
sentences.en: That's why they didn't understand everything, although they did understand most of it.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Because of that understood they not everything, although they the most well understood.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Daardoor" is a conjunction meaning "because of that" or "as a result." It often indicates causality.  
• "Verstonden" and "begrepen" are both past tense verbs. "Verstonden" is the past tense of "verstaan" (to understand, usually in the context of hearing) and "begrepen" is the past tense of "begrijpen" (to understand, usually in the context of comprehension).  
• "Hoewel" means "although" and is used to introduce a contrasting statement.  

Extra phrases/sentences:  
• "Daardoor kwam hij te laat." (As a result, he arrived late.)  
• "Hoewel het regende, gingen we wandelen." (Although it was raining, we went for a walk.)  
• "Ze verstonden de leraar niet goed." (They didn't understand the teacher well.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Daardoor kon hij niet op tijd komen, hoewel hij het geprobeerd heeft." (Because of that, he couldn't arrive on time, although he tried.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No specific culture note.

sentences.nl: En natuurlijk hielp Marieke de studenten, af en toe.
sentences.en: And of course, Marieke helped the students, occasionally.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And naturally helped Marieke the students, now and then.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses inverted word order because it begins with "En natuurlijk," placing the verb "hielp" (helped) before the subject "Marieke."  
• "Af en toe" is a common phrase meaning "now and then" or "occasionally."  
• Example 1: "Toen kwam de trein, eindelijk." (Then came the train, finally.)  
• Example 2: "Soms eet ik ijs, vooral in de zomer." (Sometimes I eat ice cream, especially in the summer.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• En soms speelt hij gitaar, in het park. (And sometimes he plays guitar, in the park.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The phrase "af en toe" is commonly used in everyday conversation in Dutch to indicate a frequency that is more sporadic than "soms" (sometimes) but still regular enough to be notable.

sentences.nl: Ook namen de studenten veel foto’s.
sentences.en: The students also took many photos.

sentences.nl: Zo konden ze zich op de spreekbeurt voorbereiden.
sentences.en: That way, they could prepare for the presentation.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• So could they themselves on the presentation prepare.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Zo" means "so" or "this way" and is used to indicate manner or method.  
• "Konden" is the past tense of "kunnen" (can) and is used here to indicate ability in the past.  
• "Zich voorbereiden" is a reflexive verb phrase meaning "to prepare oneself." The reflexive pronoun "zich" is necessary for this verb.  
• "Op de spreekbeurt" uses the preposition "op" which in this context means "for" or "on" the presentation.

Examples:  
– "Zo kon hij de taak voltooien." (So he could complete the task.)  
– "Ze konden zich op het examen concentreren." (They could concentrate on the exam.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Zo konden ze zich op de reis voorbereiden." (So they could prepare for the trip.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The word "spreekbeurt" is commonly used in Dutch schools for presentations or speaking assignments, which are a regular part of the curriculum to help students develop public speaking skills.

sentences.nl: Na de rondleiding bleven ze nog even in Orvelte.
sentences.en: After the tour, they stayed a little longer in Orvelte.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• After the tour stayed they still a little in Orvelte.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Na de rondleiding" (After the tour) uses "na" as a preposition indicating time.  
• "Bleven ze" (they stayed) shows inversion, a common word order in Dutch where the subject follows the verb in main clauses after adverbs or adverbial phrases.  
• "Nog even" (still a little) is an idiomatic expression often used to indicate a short, indefinite amount of time.  

Extra examples:  
• "Na het concert gingen ze naar huis." (After the concert, they went home.)  
• "Hij bleef nog even praten." (He stayed to chat a little longer.)  
• "Na de les gingen we koffie drinken." (After the lesson, we went to have coffee.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Na de film bleven ze nog even praten in de foyer." (After the movie, they stayed a little longer to chat in the lobby.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Orvelte is a small village in the Netherlands known for its well-preserved historic buildings and traditional Dutch atmosphere, often attracting tourists who want to experience a piece of Dutch history.

sentences.nl: Ze liepen door het dorp, behalve Gianluca en Xing.
sentences.en: They walked through the village, except Gianluca and Xing.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• They walked through the village, except Gianluca and Xing.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ze liepen" is in the past tense (imperfect) and follows the subject-verb order typical in Dutch.  
• "door het dorp" is a prepositional phrase meaning "through the village." "Door" is a preposition that indicates movement through a space.  
• "behalve" means "except," and it is used to exclude certain elements from a group. 

Extra examples:  
• Zij fietsten door de stad. (They biked through the city.)  
• Iedereen kwam naar het feest, behalve Peter. (Everyone came to the party, except Peter.)  
• Ze reisden door Europa. (They traveled through Europe.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Ze speelden in het park, behalve Anna en Tom. (They played in the park, except Anna and Tom.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The mention of names like Gianluca and Xing indicates a multicultural context, reflecting the diversity found in modern Dutch society where people from different backgrounds live together.

sentences.nl: Zij zaten op het terras.
sentences.en: They were sitting on the terrace.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• They sat on the terrace.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Zij zaten" is the past tense of "zitten" (to sit). The verb form "zaten" indicates a plural subject in the past tense.  
• "Op het terras" means "on the terrace." The preposition "op" is used for surfaces or locations.  
• Example phrases:  
  - "Hij zat op de bank." (He sat on the couch.)  
  - "Wij zaten in het park." (We sat in the park.)  
  - "Zij zaten aan tafel." (They sat at the table.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Zij zaten in de tuin. (They sat in the garden.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, sitting on a terrace is a popular activity, especially in good weather. Cafés and restaurants with terraces are common, and people enjoy sitting outside to socialize and enjoy meals or drinks.

sentences.nl: Gianluca at een ijsje, en Xing dronk een wijntje.
sentences.en: Gianluca ate an ice cream, and Xing drank a glass of wine.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Gianluca ate an ice cream, and Xing drank a little wine.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The verbs "at" (ate) and "dronk" (drank) are in the simple past tense. Dutch often uses the simple past for narrative sequences.  
• "Een ijsje" means "an ice cream," where "ijsje" is the diminutive form of "ijs" (ice, ice cream), making it sound more casual or endearing.  
• "Een wijntje" is similar, where "wijntje" is the diminutive of "wijn" (wine), often used to indicate a small or casual amount.  
• Sentence structure: Subject + verb + object, both clauses are joined by "en" (and).

  - Hij at een broodje. (He ate a sandwich.)
  - Zij dronk een kopje koffie. (She drank a cup of coffee.)
  - We gingen naar een feestje. (We went to a party.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Maria las een boek, en Jeroen keek naar een film. (Maria read a book, and Jeroen watched a movie.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, it's common to use diminutives like "ijsje" and "wijntje" to convey a sense of coziness or informality, which is a part of the Dutch concept of "gezelligheid" (coziness or conviviality).

sentences.nl: Xing vroeg aan Gianluca:, Waarom ben je zo intensief woordjes aan het leren? — Ik wil alle woorden van het woordenboek kennen.
sentences.en: Xing asked Gianluca, "Why are you studying words so intensively?" — "I want to know all the words in the dictionary."
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Xing asked to Gianluca: "Why are you so intensively words learning?" — "I want all words of the dictionary to know."

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• **Word Order:** The question "Waarom ben je zo intensief woordjes aan het leren?" uses the present continuous structure "aan het + infinitive" to indicate an ongoing action.  
• **Intensifiers:** "Zo intensief" uses "zo" to intensify the adjective "intensief" (intensive).  
• **Preposition Use:** "aan" in "vroeg aan" is used to indicate the indirect object of the verb, similar to "asked to" in English.  

Examples:  
– "Hij is aan het koken." (He is cooking.)  
– "Waarom ben je zo blij?" (Why are you so happy?)  
– "Zij vroeg aan de leraar om hulp." (She asked the teacher for help.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Lisa vroeg aan Tom: 'Wanneer ga je eindelijk het boek lezen?' — 'Ik wil het boek deze week uitlezen.'" (Lisa asked Tom: "When are you finally going to read the book?" — "I want to finish the book this week.")

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch educational settings, vocabulary learning ("woordjes leren") is often emphasized, especially in language classes, as it is seen as a fundamental way to build language proficiency.

sentences.nl: Maar waarom? — Kun je niet beter de woordjes van de les leren? — Marieke vindt het romantisch,, als ik het woordenboek uit mijn hoofd leer.
sentences.en: But why? — Wouldn't it be better to learn the words from the lesson? — Marieke finds it romantic if I memorize the dictionary.

sentences.nl: Huh…
sentences.en: Huh...

sentences.nl: Maar Gianluca…
sentences.en: But Gianluca…

sentences.nl: Jij en Marieke? — Shht… niet doorvertellen!
sentences.en: You and Marieke? — Shh… don't tell anyone!

sentences.nl: Nou… het wordt steeds spannender.
sentences.en: Well... it's getting more and more exciting.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Well… it gets more exciting.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Nou" is an interjection similar to "well" in English, often used to express hesitation or transition.  
• "Het wordt" is the present tense of "worden," meaning "to become" or "to get." It's used to indicate change.  
• "Steeds" means "more and more" or "increasingly." It emphasizes a gradual process.  
• "Spannender" is the comparative form of "spannend," meaning "exciting." In Dutch, comparatives are often formed by adding "-er" to the adjective.

Extra phrases:  
- Het wordt steeds kouder. (It is getting colder and colder.)  
- De situatie wordt steeds ingewikkelder. (The situation is becoming more and more complicated.)  
- Hij wordt steeds beter in voetbal. (He is getting better and better at soccer.)

## 3. Create a New Example
